tools.name: session_job
tools.title: Session-Attached Job
tools.description: Progress meter on THIS HAPI session for work that OUTLIVES the agent turn. Own-session only. CRITICAL: do NOT use action=set — it is refused. HYGIENE: call action=list on session start/resume AND before claiming done or inviting archive. If list shows status=running but the process is dead / you cannot prove it is alive, action=clear or update status=failed — do not ask the operator to clean meters. Leave live jobs with fresh heartbeats alone. To START a long job, use the Shell tool with: hapi job run <session-id> <job-key> --label "<label>" --progress unknown|fraction|until … -- <cmd>… (required --progress: unknown=stripes; fraction=remaining+total|done+total; until=--until <iso> with auto remaining on heartbeats). Fraction without a continuous updater freezes — keep updating done/remaining. (use "$HAPI_SESSION_ID" only when it matches the operator /sessions/<id> chat row; remote Cursor: pass the URL uuid explicitly) (auto-heartbeats + completed/failed on exit). Idle agents cannot heartbeat. This MCP tool: action=update (progress/status), action=clear, action=list only. Fraction counts need continuous update/feeder; omit counts when unknown (use --progress unknown). Never invent a percent or ETA. Not for todos, thinking, or short tool calls.

action.description: set=REFUSED (use Shell hapi job run). update=heartbeat/progress/status; clear=remove; list=show jobs

jobKey.description: Stable job key (alnum . _ -). Required for update/clear.

label.description: Ignored for MCP set (refused). Optional on update.

status.description: Job status on update (completed|failed to finish).

done.description: Units completed (pair with total). Pass null to clear a stale done count.

total.description: Total units when both ends of a fraction exist. Pass null to clear.

remaining.description: Units left. Pass null to clear so done/total can take over (web prefers remaining).

unit.description: Unit label (tracks, folders, files, …). Pass null to clear.

detail.description: Stage / current item text (not an ETA). Pass null to clear.

expectedRunId.description: Run generation fence for update/clear. Required when a manual wrapper stamped runId on set.

startedAt.description: Not used over MCP (set is refused). Correct clocks via CLI job set --started-at.

tools.name: ping_peer
tools.title: Ping Peer Session
tools.description: Send a message to another HAPI session (peer handoff / nudge). Resolves by session id prefix, then POSTs on the same hub/namespace. When the user cites a peer via [title](/sessions/<id>), Copy-reference prose See session "…" (/sessions/<id>) for context, or a bare /sessions/<id>, extract <id> and pass it as sessionIdPrefix. /sessions/<id> is a hub path - do NOT search the local filesystem for it. Prefer this (or `hapi ping-peer`) over reinventing JWT+curl. Targets another session - not the current chat. Never invent peer titles. Copy [title](/sessions/<uuid>) from the handoff or inspect_peer / search_peers - UUID is identity; rename is a non-event. Message only peers tied to your current task: a session the user cited, your Parent, or peers you spawned or were handed off to. Never broadcast to a list of peers - not for status updates, and not to announce exclusive work (simulator, device, port, branch, release). For any other peer, call inspect_peer first to see its machine, cwd, and recent work, and message it only when that work actually conflicts with or depends on yours (e.g. same machine and resource, same checkout). Do not wake inactive peers for FYI, status, or done notes. Select deliveryMode: auto (default): steer an active turn when the target supports steering and is ready; otherwise queue. Queue and auto wake hibernated peers even with wake=false. Other inactive peers require wake=true. Steer never wakes a peer. Prefer auto for routine collaboration when queueing is an acceptable fallback. If steering cannot be confirmed after acceptance, auto retains the same single accepted message without resending; accepted does not confirm consumption. queue: explicitly defer non-urgent updates that can wait instead of steering. steer: use for important, time-sensitive findings the peer needs to know now, not after finishing its current turn (e.g. a correction that invalidates its assumptions, a blocker, or a result that changes its next action). State why the finding matters now and what the peer should adjust. Steer requires insertion into an active Claude, Pi, Codex, OpenCode, Antigravity, or Cursor ACP turn; unsupported, idle, or inactive targets are rejected before sending. Steering does not abort the current turn or guarantee an immediate response. If send or steer is unconfirmed after submission, inspect the target before retrying; do not resend automatically.

sessionIdPrefix.description: Target HAPI session id or unique prefix (not this chat). Prefer full UUID from [title](/sessions/<id>) or Copy-reference. UUID only - no invented titles.

message.description: Message text to deliver to the target session

deliveryMode.description: auto (default): steer an active turn when the target supports steering and is ready; otherwise queue. Queue and auto wake hibernated peers even with wake=false. Other inactive peers require wake=true. Steer never wakes a peer. Prefer auto for routine collaboration when queueing is an acceptable fallback. If steering cannot be confirmed after acceptance, auto retains the same single accepted message without resending; accepted does not confirm consumption. queue: explicitly defer non-urgent updates that can wait instead of steering. steer: use for important, time-sensitive findings the peer needs to know now, not after finishing its current turn (e.g. a correction that invalidates its assumptions, a blocker, or a result that changes its next action). State why the finding matters now and what the peer should adjust. Steer requires insertion into an active Claude, Pi, Codex, OpenCode, Antigravity, or Cursor ACP turn; unsupported, idle, or inactive targets are rejected before sending. Steering does not abort the current turn or guarantee an immediate response. If send or steer is unconfirmed after submission, inspect the target before retrying; do not resend automatically.

wake.description: Default false. Queue and auto wake hibernated peers even with wake=false. Other inactive peers require wake=true. Steer never wakes a peer. Set true only when the user asked you to wake that peer or the work you hand off requires it to act; never for FYI, status, or done notes.

waitForReply.description: Post the peer's reply into this session when its turn ends (default false). End your turn after calling; do not poll.

tools.name: spawn_peer
tools.title: Spawn Peer Session
tools.description: Spawn a new HAPI session and deliver a required first user message (the remit). Optional machine selects the target runner (UUID or hostname from GET /api/machines); omit to use this host. directory must exist on the target machine (local existence is not required for cross-host spawns). Creates the session, optionally names it, then uses the same delivery path as ping_peer. Returns the new sessionId + name. Fails if the remit does not land (a sessionId with 0 user messages is a failed spawn). Do not call POST /api/machines/.../spawn with a message field - the hub rejects it. Use spawn_peer to create and deliver the remit. Prefer this (or `hapi spawn-peer`) over JWT+curl. Same hub/namespace as this session. Default permissionMode is yolo via hub peerSpawnDefaults / stock - omit the field to keep that default so peers work without approval prompts. Pass permissionMode only to tighten (e.g. default/plan) or when the operator names a mode; do not clone the parent session's mode. When agent/model are omitted, resolves from hub peerSpawnDefaults (Settings → General → Agents), then stock (claude + sonnet). In-session calls auto-stamp a durable Parent [title](/sessions/<uuid>) chip for this session onto the remit (fail-closed if parent id is missing). Never invent peer titles. Copy [title](/sessions/<uuid>) from the handoff or inspect_peer / search_peers - UUID is identity; rename is a non-event.

directory.description: Working directory for the new session on the target machine (must exist there)

message.description: Required first user message (the remit). Empty spawn is a failed spawn.

machine.description: Optional target runner: hub machine UUID or hostname (metadata.host / displayName from GET /api/machines). Omit to spawn on this host.

agent.description: Agent flavor override. When omitted, uses hub peerSpawnDefaults then stock claude.

model.description: Model override for the resolved agent flavor.

sessionType.description: simple or worktree. Default simple (use directory as cwd). worktree creates a new tree from directory, which must be a git repository.

permissionMode.description: Permission mode for the new session. Omit to use hub/stock default (yolo). Pass only to tighten or when the operator names a mode — do not clone the parent session.

waitForReply.description: Post the peer's reply into this session when its turn ends (default false). End your turn after calling; do not poll.

tools.name: inspect_peer
tools.title: Inspect Peer Session
tools.description: Read another HAPI session (metadata + recent message text) on the same hub/namespace. Fires when the user cites a peer via markdown [title](/sessions/<id>), Copy-reference prose See session "…" (/sessions/<id>) for context, or a bare /sessions/<id>. Extract <id> and pass it as sessionIdPrefix. /sessions/<id> is a hub path - do NOT Grep, Glob, or Read it as a local filesystem path. Read-only: does not resume. Shows machine, cwd, and recent work - call it before messaging a peer you are not already working with. Prefer this (or `hapi inspect-peer`) over JWT+curl. Never invent peer titles; always use the /sessions/<uuid> from the citation.

sessionIdPrefix.description: Target HAPI session id or unique prefix (not this chat). Prefer full UUID from [title](/sessions/<id>) or Copy-reference. UUID only - no invented titles.

messageLimit.description: Recent message page size (default 30, max 100). Text snippets only.

tools.name: list_peers
tools.title: List Peer Sessions
tools.description: Find a specific peer HAPI session on the same hub/namespace: id, active, busy/idle, flavor, machine, cwd, name. Active sessions only unless includeInactive. Uses this session's hub credentials - works from runner-spawned agents without being on the hub host. Prefer this over shelling `hapi ping-peer --list`. This is a directory, not a recipient list: Message only peers tied to your current task: a session the user cited, your Parent, or peers you spawned or were handed off to. Never broadcast to a list of peers - not for status updates, and not to announce exclusive work (simulator, device, port, branch, release). For any other peer, call inspect_peer first to see its machine, cwd, and recent work, and message it only when that work actually conflicts with or depends on yours (e.g. same machine and resource, same checkout). Do not wake inactive peers for FYI, status, or done notes.

limit.description: Max sessions to return (default 30, max 100). Newest updatedAt first.

includeInactive.description: Also list inactive sessions (default false: active only). Inactive rows are history, not recipients.
